To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rat cytomegaloviruses (RCMV) can infect and replicate in rat granulocytes (GRN) and monocytes (MONO) in vitro and that intravenous injection of RCMV-infested GRN and MONO results in systemic infection.
rat cytomegaloviruses can be transmitted from infected fibroblasts to granulocytes and macrophages, and that the infected granulocytes and/or macrophages can disseminate the virus in vivo.
RCMV can be transferred to rat monocytes and granulocytes in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the investigation of the pathogenesis of rat cytomegaloviral infection.
the development of an experimental model to study the role of leukocytes as vehicles of cytomegalavirus dissemination.
the role of leukocytes for RCMV dissemination and the establishment of an in vivo infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the present study indicate that the granulocytic lineage is involved in the in vivo spread of RCMV, whereas monocytes are not.
RCMV-infested rat leukocytes can be a source for the development of a CMV infection in rats.
the granulocyte and monocyte system is a major reservoir for the virus and that these cells are involved in CMV dissemination in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established an efficient in vitro model for the transfer of CMV to rat monocytes and granulocytes.

we could show that rat cytomegaloviruses can be transferred to rat leukocytes in vitro, that these leukocytes can be used to infect rats, that leukocytes are the main target cells for RCMV in vivo and that RCMV-infested leukocytes are the most probable source for the systemic infection of rats.
the in vitro infection of granulocytes and macrophages with RCMV is a useful model to gain insight in the role of these cells in CMV infection in vivo.

leukocytes play an important role in the in vivo spread of cytomegalova
leukocytes are important in the in vivo transfer of cytomegaliviruses, and they may play a key role in the development of CMV infection and the pathogenesis of CMV disease.
RCMV is a suitable model for studying the role of leukocytes during CMV infection.
